hypotheses.description: The synthetic intervention's observed viability effect in cell-a is attributable to incomplete perturbation of SYNTHETIC_TARGET, such that residual target activity sustains the phenotype.
The synthetic intervention's observed viability effect in cell-a is attributable to multi-target activity, such that engagement of targets beyond SYNTHETIC_TARGET contributes to the phenotype.

differing_assumptions: Hypothesis a assumes the intervention engages SYNTHETIC_TARGET but does not fully suppress its activity; hypothesis b assumes the intervention engages additional targets that contribute to viability.
Hypothesis a treats residual SYNTHETIC_TARGET activity as sufficient to sustain viability; hypothesis b treats off-target engagement as a necessary contributor to the viability phenotype.
The two hypotheses make different predictions about whether increasing target engagement alone would alter viability versus whether altering the multi-target profile would alter viability.
interpretation_boundaries: The planned flat synthetic assay is an engineering fixture and cannot establish any biological mechanism, regulatory edge, causal effect, or efficacy claim.

The planned result cannot distinguish whether any observed response reflects incomplete perturbation, multi-target activity, or another unmeasured process; it can only return the registered outcome categories a or b.
No biological proof is established by this fixture; any interpretation beyond the synthetic outcome category is outside the scope of the planned result.
